children: Germany's governing coalition could see its room for maneuver squeezed by a weak performance in coming regional elections, Alexander Valentin at Oxford Economics warns. The far-right AfD is projected to make gains at elections in three states in Europe's most important economy in September, possibly winning a majority in at least one. That move away from the center dominated by the ruling coalition could spread to other, larger states voting next year, Valentin writes in a note. "We see an increasing risk of a political stalemate at the national level that would derail necessary reforms and could prompt us to revise Germany's potential growth downwards," he says.
